text: Now some men from among the elders of Israel came to me and sat down before me.

versions.text: Some of the elders of Israel came to me and sat down before me.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has אֲנָשִׁים מִזִּקְנֵי ("men from among the elders"); rendering the noun makes the partitive clearer, and the opening connective helps the oral flow into the following verse.

text: Then the word of the LORD came to me:
"Son of man, these men have taken their idols into their hearts and set the stumbling block of their guilt before their faces. Should I let myself be consulted by them at all?

Therefore speak to them and say: This is what the Lord GOD says: Any Israelite who takes his idols into his heart and sets the stumbling block of his guilt before his face, and then comes to the prophet—I, the LORD, will answer him myself, in keeping with his many idols,
so that I may lay hold of the house of Israel by their own hearts, for they have all turned away from me through their idols.
Therefore say to the house of Israel: This is what the Lord GOD says: Repent! Turn away from your idols, and turn your faces from all your abominations.

For any Israelite, or any foreigner residing in Israel, who separates himself from me and takes his idols into his heart, setting the stumbling block of his guilt before his face, and then comes to the prophet to inquire of me—I, the LORD, will answer him myself.
I will set my face against that man; I will make him a sign and a byword, and I will cut him off from among my people. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
And if the prophet is deceived and speaks a word, I, the LORD, have deceived that prophet; I will stretch out my hand against him and destroy him from among my people Israel.
They will bear their guilt—the guilt of the one who inquires will be the same as the guilt of the prophet—
so that the house of Israel may no longer stray from me and no longer defile themselves with all their transgressions. Then they will be my people, and I will be their God, declares the Lord GOD."
The word of the LORD came to me:
"Son of man, if a land sins against me by acting unfaithfully, and I stretch out my hand against it and break its staff of bread, sending famine upon it and cutting off from it both man and beast,
then even if these three men—Noah, Daniel, and Job—were in it, they would save only their own lives by their righteousness, declares the Lord GOD.
Or if I let wild beasts pass through that land and they leave it bereft of its children, so that it becomes desolate, with no one passing through because of the beasts,

versions.text: Or if I send wild beasts through that land and they leave it childless, so that it becomes a wasteland where no one passes through because of the beasts,
versions.explanation: "Leave it childless" is awkward when spoken of a land; the verb שִׁכֵּל means to bereave of children. Also, שְׁמָמָה is rendered "desolate" in verse 16, so consistent wording aids oral coherence.

text: then as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, even if these three men were in it, they could not save their own sons or daughters. They alone would be saved, and the land would be desolate.
Or if I bring the sword against that land and say, 'Let the sword sweep through the land,' and I cut off from it both man and beast,
then as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, even if these three men were in it, they could not save their own sons or daughters; they alone would be saved.
Or if I send a plague into that land and pour out my wrath upon it in bloodshed, cutting off from it both man and beast,
then as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, they could not save a son or a daughter; by their righteousness they would save only their own lives.
For this is what the Lord GOD says: How much worse will it be when I send my four dreadful judgments against Jerusalem—sword and famine, wild beasts and plague—to cut off from it both man and beast!

Yet some survivors will be left in it, sons and daughters who will be brought out. They will come out to you, and when you see their conduct and their deeds, you will be consoled concerning the disaster I have brought upon Jerusalem—everything I have brought upon it.
They will console you when you see their conduct and their deeds, and you will know that I have done nothing in it without cause, declares the Lord GOD."
